title: ～んだって — “I hear that ～” (casual)
summary: A casual way to pass on something you heard from someone else. It is the spoken equivalent of ～そうだ (hearsay). It follows the plain form and is used between friends and family.

patterns.form: 動詞・イ形容詞 普通形＋んだって
patterns.gloss: plain form + んだって (結婚するんだって)

patterns.form: ナ形容詞・名詞＋なんだって
patterns.gloss: na-adjective or noun + なんだって (学生なんだって)

body.p: It is the spoken explanatory んだ (from のだ) plus the quotation marker って. Like ～んだそうだ, it passes along what someone else said. Na-adjectives and nouns take なんだって.

Use it in talk with friends and family. For a polite version, use 〜そうです or 〜ということです. With rising intonation, 〜なんだって？ can also be a question checking what you heard. Use it only for information you were told, not for facts you confirmed yourself.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）、来月（らいげつ）結婚（けっこん）するんだって。
examples.tr: I heard he's getting married next month.
examples.note: Verb plain form + んだって.

examples.ja: あの店（みせ）のラーメン、すごくおいしいんだって。
examples.romaji: Ano mise no rāmen, sugoku oishii ndatte.
examples.tr: I hear the ramen at that shop is really delicious.
examples.note: I-adjective plain form + んだって.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）から、この道（みち）は工事（こうじ）で通（とお）れないんだって。
examples.romaji: Ashita kara, kono michi wa kōji de tōrenai ndatte.
examples.tr: I hear this road will be closed for construction from tomorrow.
examples.note: Negative plain form + んだって.

pitfalls: With na-adjectives and nouns, だ becomes な: 学生なんだって, not 学生んだって.
It is casual. With superiors or in formal situations, use 〜そうです.
